hints: Use $R^2=5+4$ and $\tan\alpha=2/\sqrt5$, then respect the stated acute range for $\alpha$.
walkthrough:
Equate $(\sqrt{5})\cos x + 2\sin x$ to the expanded form $R\cos(x - \alpha) = R\cos x\cos\alpha + R\sin x\sin\alpha$:
$$R\cos\alpha = \sqrt{5}$$
$$R\sin\alpha = 2$$

Square and add both equations to calculate $R$:
$$R^2 = (R\cos\alpha)^2 + (R\sin\alpha)^2 = (\sqrt{5})^2 + 2^2 = 5 + 4 = 9$$
Since $R > 0$:
$$R = \sqrt{9} = 3$$

Divide the two equations to find $\tan\alpha$:
$$\tan\alpha = \dfrac{R\sin\alpha}{R\cos\alpha} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$$

State $R$ and the value of $\alpha$ correct to 2 decimal places:
$$R = 3, \quad \alpha = 41.81^\circ$$

hints: Apply the part (i) result with $x$ replaced by $x/2$.
Solve $3\cos(x/2-\alpha)=1.2$, so the cosine value is 0.4.
Find both general cosine branches, but retain only those for which $0^\circ<x<360^\circ$.
Use the part (i) value of $\alpha$ consistently when converting back to $x$.
walkthrough:
Use the result from part (i) with argument $\dfrac{1}{2}x$:
$$3\cos\left(\dfrac{1}{2}x - 41.8103^\circ\right) = 1.2$$

Calculate the principal angle using inverse cosine:
$$\beta = \arccos(0.4) \approx 66.4218^\circ$$

Determine the interval for the angle $\dfrac{1}{2}x - 41.8103^\circ$ when $0^\circ < x < 360^\circ$:
$$0^\circ < \dfrac{1}{2}x < 180^\circ \implies -41.81^\circ < \dfrac{1}{2}x - 41.8103^\circ < 138.19^\circ$$

The only angle in this interval where cosine equals $0.4$ is $+66.4218^\circ$:
$$\dfrac{1}{2}x - 41.8103^\circ = 66.4218^\circ$$

State the unique solution correct to 1 decimal place:
$$x = 216.5^\circ$$

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Evaluation of $\cos^{-1}(0.4)$ to at least 1 d.p. ($66.42^\circ$ to 2 d.p.). Gives $216.5^\circ$. The final result is $x=216.5^\circ$.
